mentl/7448ad4:
HandlerKind was DECLARED 5-field (handled_ename, residual_row, config,
state, arms) so the env names the handler's whole node — but the writer
(register_handler) only populated 2; the other three stayed empty. So a
name-keyed side-ledger, handler_state_inits_registry, carried (inits,
arm_names) instead, populated by a pre-register pass and read by-name via
find_registry_field's filter. The Universal Audit: that data is the
graph's, re-derived into a ledger (Carried-Truth). Worse, the by-name
filter ran INSIDE the registry handler's own arm, re-triggering the
nested-arm evidence gap it was a workaround for — m2 trapped there
compiling the wheel.

Fix, toward LESS code:
- write side (infer): populate HandlerKind(ename, r, config, state, arms).
- read side (lower): handler_decl_of reads the env's HandlerKind live;
  lookup_handler_{state_inits,arm_names}_of project (config,state)/arms
  through the same lower_state_field_inits / build_handler_arm_names the
  pre-pass used — identical values, no ledger, evaluated at the top-level
  call site instead of inside a handler arm.
- remove the effect, both handlers, the pre-register pass and its install.

Order-free resolution preserved: inference register_handlers every decl
before lower runs, so an install resolves a handler whose decl follows it
via the env, not a pre-pass.

Verified: seed compiles the wheel, micros 7/7, drift-audit clean, no
dangling refs to removed symbols. The filter-in-arm trap is gone; pass-2
marches deeper to lower_one_arm_decl -> lower_expr (the next masked site).
Sits on the in-progress type-parameterized-effects substrate (EAType,
register_effect_ops full var set, subst_ty chase-to-root); the census
baseline bump 190->201 is explained in tools/verify-baseline.txt (census
is a shadow; the fixed-point + trap-march is the oracle).

Mentl's audit, landed in one pass.

(1) __closure → __state. Closure captures and handler evidence are
both frozen handler state; both accessed by identical mechanics
(offset-load from an implicit first param into a bump-allocated
record). One implicit param with slot kinds, not two parallel
conventions. Surpasses W7/W4's "both __closure and __ev" wording;
aligned with DESIGN Ch 1 "one mechanism" and Ch 4 "handler IS state."
The state record's shape stays the same; W4 will grow evidence slots
inside it without touching the calling convention.

Affected: backends/wasm.ka (every $__closure → $__state, every
$clos_tmp → $state_tmp, ~24 sites including emit_one_function
param decl, LMakeClosure stores, LUpval offset-load, LCall arg
push, LTailCall, _start main dispatch, comments), types.ka and
lower.ka (Resolution / LowerScope comments).

(2) emit_alloc as EmitMemory effect. Anchor 5 ("if it needs to
exist, it's a handler") applied to backend memory strategy. The
effect declares emit_alloc(size, target_local) -> (); emit_memory_bump
implements the inline $heap_ptr bump; future arena / gc handlers
slot in via the same effect surface without disturbing closure
layout, list construction, or any other allocation site. DESIGN 7.3
"the handler IS the backend" extends to memory strategy. Installed
in pipeline.ka's compile chain alongside wat_stdout (which had been
declared but never installed — also fixed here).

(3) Tier-2 snoc cleanup. Walks via list_head/list_tail recursion
with ++-output construction across own.ka, clock.ka, mentl.ka all
converted to flat-indexed loops with pre-sized make_list buffers
plus list_copy_into trim. Specifically:

- own.ka: find_first_span, collect_ref_params, walk_match_arms,
  infer_ownership, count_uses_list, count_match_arms.
- clock.ka: clock_record / tick_record handler state restructured
  to (trace, trace_len) flat-buffer-plus-counter via list_extend_to;
  clock_replay / tick_replay handlers carry (trace, read_idx) and
  advance the curs
